item.title: Does Poor Sleep Lead to Injuries?
item.description: Those who reported poorer sleep on average (in response to the question “How was your sleep last night?”, on a scale of 1 to 6) were significantly more likely to subsequently get injured. In fact, for every one-point decrease in sleep quality, they were 36 percent more likely to report an injury. The post Does Poor Sleep Lead to Injuries? appeared first on Outside Online.

item.title: The One Meal Olympic Bobsledder Elana Meyers Taylor Relies on During Training
item.description: The daughter of an athlete, Elana Meyers Taylor, seemed destined for sports. At 11, she held a torch at the Atlanta Games. Decades later, she’s claimed six Olympic medals. Most recently, she took home her first gold medal in the women’s monobobsled event on Monday, February 16, at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Olympics—her fifth Games. The post The One Meal Olympic Bobsledder Elana Meyers Taylor Relies on During Training appeared first on Outside Online.

item.title: The Breakfast Olympic Freestyle Skier Ashley Caldwell Eats to Power Her Training
item.description: “Breakfast burritos are a solid way to start the day, especially postpartum,” Caldwell said. “My body needs so much just to train and compete.
